record.original_question: Let T(a_1, a_2, ..., a_n) be a norm form written in some integral basis of a proper degree-n extension of Q. Determine all functions f: Z -> C such that T(f(a_1), f(a_2), ..., f(a_n)) depends only on the value T(a_1, a_2, ..., a_n), rather than on the specific tuple (a_1, a_2, ..., a_n).

evidence.quote: Problem 6. Let T(a_1, a_2, ..., a_n) be a norm form in some integral basis of some proper field extension of Q of degree n. Find all functions f : Z -> C, such that T(f(a_1), f(a_2), ..., f(a_n)) depends only on the value of T(a_1, a_2, ..., a_n).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $K/\mathbb{Q}$ be a proper number field of degree $n \geq 2$, and let $\omega_1, \omega_2, \ldots, \omega_n$ be a $\mathbb{Z}$-basis of its ring of integers $\mathcal{O}_K$. Define the associated norm form
$$T(a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n) := N_{K/\mathbb{Q}}(a_1 \omega_1 + a_2 \omega_2 + \cdots + a_n \omega_n) \in \mathbb{Z}[a_1, \ldots, a_n],$$
where $N_{K/\mathbb{Q}}$ denotes the field norm. 

Determine all functions $f : \mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{C}$ such that the value
$$T(f(a_1), f(a_2), \ldots, f(a_n))$$
depends only on the value of $T(a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n)$, and not on the particular choice of integer tuple $(a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n) \in \mathbb{Z}^n$ realizing that value. That is, characterize all $f$ such that whenever $T(a_1,\ldots,a_n) = T(b_1,\ldots,b_n)$ for $(a_i),(b_i)\in\mathbb{Z}^n$, one has $T(f(a_1),\ldots,f(a_n)) = T(f(b_1),\ldots,f(b_n))$.
